transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-21
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration recorded: 59 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Rowan Bell (Redwood CSM); Jared Morales (Aurelion Head of Procurement), Nina Patel (Aurelion InfoSec), Marco Ruiz (Aurelion ML Platform), Ellen Cho (Aurelion Legal)

Summary: quick procurement / legal sync to align on MSA/DPA redlines, confirm KMS and audit log expectations, discuss bandwidth/egress constraints for pilot, and define rollback / fallback playbook for Dedicated vs Hosted paths. Action items and dates captured at end.

Topics: MSA redline focus, customer-managed KMS, audit logs retention, SLA thresholds, pilot sizing and bandwidth, rollback and automatic fallback to smaller model variant, pricing approvals and billing path.

Transcript:
00:00 Liam Chen: All right hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about an hour, we'll try to be crisp. I'm Liam from Redwood, AE. Priya from SE will cover the technical bits, Rowan's on to help with onboarding planning. Jared, Nina, Marco, Ellen from Aurelion, thanks for making time.
00:22 Jared Morales: Yeah thanks Liam, appreciate it. Quick ask from procurement side, we want to map a clean path to production acceptance — what do you need from legal to unblock pricing approvals.
00:35 Liam Chen: Good question. High level: we need a signed MSA and DPA, and then the pricing annex for the committed capacity. Ellen, if you want either a redline or a mark-up, we can send a proposed MSA with clause variants for KMS, egress, and SLA credits.
00:52 Ellen Cho: Sending a proposed draft would help. There are two sticking points: one, we need clear KMS ownership language; two, limits on indemnity and audit rights.
01:08 Priya Kapoor: On the KMS side, we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/private deployments — integration patterns are either bring-your-own-KMS with HSM or we can use Redwood-managed keys with CMEK restrictions. There's a slight operational delta on rotation visibility.
01:30 Nina Patel: By slight delta do you mean Redwood still sees plaintext at some point? That's a hard stop for us. We need encryption at rest where keys are not accessible to Redwood ops.
01:45 Priya Kapoor: Yeah, fair. For private (VPC) deployments we can implement a zero-access KMS flow — the key usage happens in the customer's HSM and Redwood never stores the unencrypted keys. For hosted tiers that's trickier, we offer envelope encryption with Redwood managing the outer keys.
02:05 Marco Ruiz: So to be clear, if we do a Dedicated pool in our VPC with customer KMS, we get zero-key access and audit logs? What's the retention on those logs?
02:20 Priya Kapoor: We can push audit logs to your SIEM via Kinesis/Syslog for a configurable retention. Default retention is 90 days in the hosted console, but for private/on-prem installs we can match your retention policy — we just need the log sink/endpoint and SLAs for storage side.
02:36 Nina Patel: We need 365+ logs for initial compliance evaluation. Can that be supported?
02:42 Priya Kapoor: Yes we can support 365 retention for Private deployments; for Hosted we'd need to propose an add-on. We'll include that in the DPA appendix.
03:00 Liam Chen: Important procurement note — the pricing annex differs between Hosted (usage-based) and Dedicated (reserved commit). Jared, which path are you leaning toward?
03:12 Jared Morales: Initially we want a Hosted pilot to validate latency/cost, but long-term we want Dedicated for predictability. Procurement wants to see a migration and rollback plan so they can approve a pilot without committing to long-term spend.
03:28 Rowan Bell: We usually do a 1-week pilot with a throughput target that mimics production — we'll set a canary route, measure p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. If the numbers align, there's a templated transition to Dedicated with a 30-day opt-out for the first quarter.
03:45 Marco Ruiz: Bandwidth question — our infra caps egress to 2 Gbps per region during the pilot window. Does Redwood expect burst capacity higher than that? Any cost impact?
04:00 Priya Kapoor: Redwood's serving runtime is bursty by sequence length; sustained RPS shapes matter more than raw Gbps. We can throttle at the load balancer and implement a soft-QPS cap. For cost, egress charges are external and billed per provider, but model choice affects token count and thus egress. We'll model it in the benchmark.
04:20 Jared Morales: And rollback? If the pilot shows regression in latency, what's the default fallback?
04:28 Priya Kapoor: Two-layer rollback: at control plane level we can automatically route to a smaller-but-compatible model variant in the same region (faster, cheaper), or route to a different region with capacity. We can also degrade non-critical features like streaming chunk size. We'll document playbook steps.
04:45 Ellen Cho: From legal I need the SLA credits and a hard definition of "unavailable" — like 5 minute vs 30 minute windows. Also need to see the proposed cap on aggregate liability.
05:00 Liam Chen: Makes sense. We'll propose standard SLA: 99.9% region-level availability with credits computed monthly — will include 99/95/90 tiers in the annex. Liability cap we can propose to match customer's enterprise limits; we'll flag that for commercial.
05:18 Nina Patel: On DPA, data residency and deletion are critical. We need ability to request deletion with cert within 48 hours.
05:27 Priya Kapoor: We support expunge APIs and can produce deletion certificates. For Hosted, deletion from cold storage may take longer but we will provide a signed certificate when objects are purged per process.
05:44 Marco Ruiz: Are there any performance tradeoffs if we enable strict per-customer KV cache isolation? We want to avoid cross-tenant cache contamination.
05:55 Priya Kapoor: Per-customer cache isolation has small memory overhead but no notable latency penalty. It prevents prefix cache hits across tenants. We'll note that as a config option in the pilot.
06:12 Jared Morales: Back to pricing mapping — procurement wants a clear escalation route if pilot costs exceed forecast. Who signs off on overage?
06:22 Liam Chen: We can cap pilot spend in the billing account, and any change beyond the cap requires written PO approval. We'll include a billing threshold notification and auto-disable feature for safety.
06:38 Ellen Cho: Also need to check export control / data classification language if models are used for regulated data.
06:45 Priya Kapoor: We'll surface a model usage appendix; for regulated data we recommend private deployment or dedicated with strict egress controls.
07:00 Marco Ruiz: On competitor comparison — you mentioned Anthropic and in-house models. One blocker for us is deterministic latency; we need p95 < 350ms for short prompts at 128 tokens. Can you get close?
07:16 Priya Kapoor: For a 128-token median sequence and optimized kernel selection, we can hit p95 around 220–320ms on Dedicated NVIDIA A100-ish clusters. Hosted numbers vary by region. We'll run a short benchmark targeted to your sequence distribution.
07:35 Jared Morales: Perfect. For procurement timeline: we want legal & infosec cleared within two weeks to allow pilot next month. Is that feasible?
07:45 Liam Chen: It's tight but doable. We'll push the MSA redline out in 48 hours, Priya will send the perf plan in three business days, and Marco/Jared confirm peering windows — if all that aligns, pilot can start early July.
08:00 Ellen Cho: One more legal nuance: we prefer a single-signatory PO path for pilots under $25k. Can you accommodate simpler billing for pilot?
08:12 Liam Chen: Yes we can do a simplified PO for pilot amounts under $25k, Rowan will coordinate invoicing.
08:20 Rowan Bell: I'll follow up on billing contacts.
08:25 (noise)
08:35 Nina Patel: Slight tangent — who has access to model telemetry? We need role-based access and audit trails.
08:45 Priya Kapoor: RBAC is supported; telemetry streams can be scoped per token-level or route-level. Audit trails include token counts, latency, user IDs — we redact prompt text unless you opt-in to full logging.
09:00 Marco Ruiz: Ok that helps.
09:06 Jared Morales: Could you also include a short statement on disaster recovery SLA? If a region goes down we need a documented RTO and RPO.
09:16 Liam Chen: We'll add an RTO/RPO appendix; typical regional failover is sub-30 minutes to route to alternate region for stateless routes. For stateful workloads with KV cache we document replication windows.
09:35 Ellen Cho: Anything else from Redwood side?
09:40 Priya Kapoor: We'll include a migration/rollback checklist: health check thresholds, canary sample size, manual cutover steps, automatic fallback triggers — we'll attach that as a one-pager.
09:56 Liam Chen: Great. Recap time — quick bullets: Redwood to send MSA redline and proposed DPA appendix with KMS and log retention options; SE to run perf bench and share numbers; customer to confirm peering/bandwidth; legal to mark DPA redlines; procurement to confirm pilot PO path.
10:20 Jared Morales: Sounds right. We'll aim to have legal and infosec notes back by 2026-06-29.
10:35 Liam Chen: Excellent. Anything else?
10:40 Marco Ruiz: Maybe a short question — if pilot passes, what's typical lead time to Dedicated capacity?
10:48 Liam Chen: Typically 2–4 weeks from signed commit depending on GPU inventory and region; we can offer burst capacity in the interim for crucial windows.
11:05 Ellen Cho: If you can get the MSA redline in two days we'll expedite our review.
11:12 Liam Chen: We'll do that. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
11:20 (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription had occasional misheard words; speaker labels were validated by organizer post-call. Audio had a brief dropout at 08:25–08:35 UTC (~10s).

End of transcript.
